props.gloss_en: the mishna: one who chisels and one who strikes with a hammer or with an adze ... is liable (listed as two)
the mishna: one who drills any amount is liable
Rav: one who chisels is liable on account of building
Shmuel: one who chisels is liable on account of striking with a hammer
Rav: one who makes a hole in a chicken coop is liable on account of building
Shmuel: one who makes a hole in a chicken coop is liable on account of striking with a hammer
Rav: one who inserts a pin into the handle of a hoe is liable on account of building
Shmuel: one who inserts a pin into the handle of a hoe is liable on account of striking with a hammer

had it taught the first [chiseling] only: there Rav says [building] because that is the way of building; but a hole in a chicken coop, which is not the way of building, say he agrees with Shmuel -- so the coop dispute teaches Rav says building even there

had it taught this [the coop] only: there Rav says [building] because it resembles building, being made for ventilation; but a pin in a hoe handle, which is not the way of building, say he agrees with Shmuel -- so the hoe dispute teaches Rav says building even there

had it taught this [the hoe] only: there Shmuel says [hammer], but in those two say he agrees with Rav -- so the chiseling and coop disputes teach Shmuel says hammer even there. [All three are] necessary
here we are dealing with one who bored it with an iron nail and left it inside it, which is the completion of the labour

answered_by.gloss_en: אימא: המסתת המכה בפטיש -- read: one who chisels [is liable as] one who strikes with a hammer
